summary: Extends the Sieve mail filtering language with the ability to check whether a mailbox exists, read mailbox and server metadata annotations, and control whether fileinto creates a mailbox that is missing. It builds on the base Sieve language in RFC 5228.

eli5.summary: Sieve is a set of rules that sorts your email into folders. This note lets those rules check whether a folder exists, read notes about folders, and create the folder if it is missing.

questions: how to check if a mailbox exists in sieve
what is the sieve mailbox extension
subtitle: New Sieve tests that check whether a mailbox exists, read mailbox and server annotations, and create missing folders.

tldr.problem: Sieve scripts could not check whether a mailbox exists, read annotations set through the IMAP METADATA extension, or ask for a mailbox to be created when filing a message.
tldr.mechanism: Three extensions add tests (mailboxexists, metadata, metadataexists, servermetadata, servermetadataexists) and a :create argument for fileinto, each enabled through a require capability string.
tldr.outcome: Scripts can change behavior based on mailbox state and annotations. The tests are read-only and cannot modify annotations.

today: RFC 5490 is a Proposed Standard. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
This memo extends the Sieve mail filtering language from RFC 5228 so scripts can access mailbox and server annotations. This lets a Sieve engine's behavior be customized by values set using the IMAP METADATA extension in RFC 5464.

It also defines an extension for checking whether a mailbox exists and for controlling mailbox creation on the fileinto action. Readers are assumed to know the data model and terms in section 3 of RFC 5464. The author thanks the Open Mobile Alliance's Mobile Email working group for requirements from mobile devices that guided some of the extensions.
sections.eli5: This note gives the mail-sorting helper a few new abilities, like peeking at notes attached to folders.

sections.title: Checking and Creating Mailboxes
sections.content:
The mailboxexists test takes a list of mailbox names. It is true if all of them exist in the mailstore and each allows the user running the script to deliver messages into it. For an IMAP server, delivery is possible if the READ-WRITE response code is present (when the Access Control List extension is not supported), or the user has the 'p' or 'i' rights for the mailbox.

A true result does not guarantee that fileinto will succeed. For example, the user might be over quota. The test only checks existence and permission.

The :create argument to fileinto tells the interpreter to create the mailbox, if needed, before delivering. If the mailbox already exists the argument is ignored. Failure to create the mailbox is an error. Both features use the capability string mailbox.
sections.eli5: The helper can ask, "Is there a folder called Partners?" and can also make the folder before putting a letter in it.

sections.title: Mailbox Metadata Tests
sections.content:
The mboxmetadata capability adds two tests. metadata retrieves the value of a named annotation on a named mailbox and compares it to a list of keys. It is true if the annotation exists and its value matches any of the keys. The default match type is :is and the default comparator is i;ascii-casemap.

metadataexists takes a mailbox and a list of annotation names. It is true if all of the annotations exist, meaning they have non-NIL values.

Annotations MUST be accessed with the permissions of the user running the script, and annotations starting with /private MUST be those of that user.

In the RFC's example, a script checks the INBOX annotation /private/vendor/vendor.isode/auto-replies. If it equals on, the script sends a vacation reply.
sections.eli5: Each folder can have little sticky notes. The helper can read a note, such as "auto-reply: on", and act on it.

sections.title: Server Metadata Tests
sections.content:
The servermetadata capability works like the mailbox version but for annotations on the server as a whole. The servermetadata test retrieves a server annotation and compares it to a key list, with the same defaults (:is and i;ascii-casemap). The servermetadataexists test is true if all listed server annotations exist with non-NIL values.

The same permission rules apply: access uses the running user's permissions, and /private annotations belong to that user.

The RFC's example reads /private/vendor/vendor.isode/notification-uri into a variable, then, if it is not none, builds a notification message from the envelope sender, the Subject header and the From address. It combines this extension with the variables, enotify and envelope extensions, which are not required to implement this one.
sections.eli5: Besides notes on folders, there can be notes on the whole mail server. The helper can read those too, for example to find where to send a notification.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extensions deliberately provide no way to modify annotations. A failure to retrieve annotations, such as the storing server being down, may change the result of Sieve processing. Implementations SHOULD treat a temporary failure to retrieve annotations the same way as a temporary failure to retrieve the Sieve script. Annotations should be treated as a part of the script itself.

Protocols and APIs used to retrieve annotations MUST provide at least the same level of confidentiality as those used to retrieve Sieve scripts. For example, if scripts come from LDAP secured with TLS, annotations must be fetched by a comparably protected mechanism.
sections.eli5: The helper can only read the notes, never change them. If it cannot reach the notes, it should act as if it could not reach its rule list either.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA has added three registrations to the list of Sieve extensions. Each names a capability a script lists in its require command, and the contact address is the Sieve discussion list.

  • mailbox: the mailbox existence test and the :create argument to fileinto.
  • mboxmetadata: tests for mailbox metadata existence and value retrieval.
  • servermetadata: tests for server metadata existence and value retrieval.
sections.eli5: The three new abilities were written in an official list so everyone uses the same names for them.
